title: Document

blocks.verbatim_text:
Use the document-generate skill to sync the prose doc set to what actually shipped — all four
Diataxis quadrants: tutorial, how-to, reference, explanation. Source it from SPEC/spec.md,
docs/global/architecture/SDD.md's ADRs, and the phase PLAN files, so trade-offs and
alternatives-considered come from the ADR that already recorded them rather than being
re-derived from code comments and git history.
blocks.surrounding_prose: Header: '## 14. Document — while the PR is still open'. Preamble: 'These run in sequence, one paste at a time.' content-qa rewrites prose, so it cannot run beside doc-verifier — the verifier would be checking text that is still being edited. Order matters: prose → code-level docs → release → de-slop → verify. Also: 'document-generate and code-documenter are sequential, not alternatives — their surfaces do not overlap. document-generate writes the four Diataxis quadrants and nothing else; it does not touch docstrings or API specs. code-documenter writes docstrings, JSDoc/TSDoc and OpenAPI/AsyncAPI and nothing else; it has no Diataxis quadrants. Running only one leaves half the doc set unwritten.' This is the first block in the sequence (prose).

blocks.verbatim_text:
Now use the code-documenter skill for the half document-generate does not cover: docstrings on
every function and class this milestone added or changed, in this project's existing convention
(Google/NumPy/Sphinx for Python, JSDoc/TSDoc for JS/TS), and the OpenAPI or AsyncAPI spec for
any endpoint or event it added or changed. Validate every example you write by actually
compiling or running it — an example that does not run is a defect, not documentation. Do not
re-open the Diataxis pages document-generate just wrote; those are its surface, not yours.
blocks.surrounding_prose: Gated by: '(skip only if this milestone shipped no code-level public surface — no new or changed functions, classes, HTTP endpoints, or published events)'. This is the code-level docs step in the sequence (prose → code-level docs → release → de-slop → verify).

blocks.verbatim_text:
Nothing on the manual path wrote a version bump or a CHANGELOG entry, so author both now,
before document-release runs. finishing-a-development-branch does neither, and document-release
will not cover for it: it skips its CHANGELOG step outright when the branch did not modify
CHANGELOG, and "overwrite, replace, or regenerate CHANGELOG entries" is on its NEVER list.
Left alone, this milestone reaches step 15 unversioned and unlogged, silently.

Enumerate every commit with `git log <base>..HEAD --oneline` and read `git diff <base>...HEAD`
to see what each one actually changed. Decide the bump level from that diff — patch for fixes
and small additive changes, minor for a new capability or a migration, major for breaking
changes; ask me before anything above patch. Write the bump to VERSION and the manifest
together, never just one of them; skip this silently if the project tracks no version at all.
Then write one unified CHANGELOG entry for the new version, dated today, in the CHANGELOG's
existing format, grouped into Added / Changed / Fixed / Removed. Lead with what the user can now
do that they could not before, not with implementation detail. Every commit in that log must map
to at least one bullet — infer them from the diff, do not ask me to describe them. Commit both
and push so the PR picks them up.

Then tell me plainly that ship's coverage-gap tracing and plan-completion audit did not run on
this path either: nothing has cross-checked this milestone's tests against its coverage gaps, or
its PHASE/VERIFICATION.md files against what was promised. That gap is mine to accept or close
by hand.
blocks.surrounding_prose: Gated by: '(only if you took the manual path at step 13)'. This block invokes no skill/agent directly — it is manual authoring instructions (git log/diff, version bump, CHANGELOG) referencing finishing-a-development-branch and document-release (upcoming) and ship (elsewhere) by name descriptively, not as invocations within this block.

blocks.verbatim_text:
Use the document-release skill. Build the shipped-vs-documented coverage map against
SPEC/spec.md's US-xxx story bank as well as the diff, so a requirement never touched at all
still gets flagged. Sync each doc against the diff, check the architecture diagrams for drift,
and polish the CHANGELOG entry that already exists — whether ship wrote it or I did on the
manual path. Polish the voice only, never rewrite or regenerate it. Run from the feature branch
with the PR still open; it aborts on the base branch because it needs the unmerged diff.
blocks.surrounding_prose: No explicit conditional gate before this block (applies to both automated and manual paths — text explicitly says 'whether ship wrote it or I did on the manual path'). This is the 'release' step in the prose → code-level docs → release → de-slop → verify sequence. Must run from the feature branch with PR still open.

blocks.verbatim_text:
Use the content-qa skill over everything this step has touched, including document-release's
own edits — AI-ism scan first, then the editorial pass. This step rewrites prose, so it runs
alone: nothing else reads or writes these files while it is working.
blocks.surrounding_prose: This is the 'de-slop' step in the sequence. Reiterates the ordering constraint from the step-14 header preamble: content-qa cannot run beside doc-verifier since it rewrites prose that doc-verifier would be checking.

blocks.verbatim_text:
Dispatch the doc-verifier agent last, now that content-qa has finished rewriting. It verifies
exactly one file per dispatch, so this is one agent per doc, not one agent for the doc set:
first list every doc this step created or touched — README, CHANGELOG, and everything under
docs/ — then dispatch one doc-verifier per doc, all in a single message. They only read the
codebase and each writes its own separate result file, so they do not collide.

Give each dispatch a <verify_assignment> block with both inputs it requires: doc_path, the doc's
path relative to the project root, and project_root, the absolute path of this repo. Leave the
output directory at its default, docs/state/tmp/.

Each agent writes docs/state/tmp/verify-<doc filename>.json and returns a one-line confirmation
and nothing else — by design it will not hand back claim detail inline, so do not ask it to.
Once they have all reported, read those JSON files yourself and give me the consolidated result:
every entry from every failures array with its doc, line, claim, expected and actual, plus the
claims_passed / claims_checked totals per doc, and a plain list of which docs came back clean.
blocks.surrounding_prose: This is the final 'verify' step in the sequence, run last, after content-qa has finished rewriting. Followed by the standalone line '**Then land it.**' which transitions to the merge/deploy blocks below.

blocks.verbatim_text:
Use the land-and-deploy skill. It picks up where ship left off: readiness gate → merge → poll
the deploy platform → verify production health, with revert as the escape hatch at every
failure point. GitHub only — on GitLab or an unrecognized platform it stops and hands off to a
manual merge, which is the correct outcome, not a failure.
blocks.surrounding_prose: Preceded by bolded transition '**Then land it.**'. Gated by: '(only if you took the automated path at step 13)'. Mentions 'ship' descriptively (what land-and-deploy picks up from), not as an invocation in this block.

blocks.verbatim_text:
Merge the PR now, with the docs in it — they land with the diff, not after it. First confirm
`gh pr checks` is green on the current head, and that nothing has been pushed to the PR since
content-qa and doc-verifier ran; if something has, the doc pass is stale, so re-run those two
before merging. Then merge with `gh pr merge` using this repo's merge method and delete the
remote branch, but leave the local worktree in place until step 15 is finished.

land-and-deploy does not run on this path, so nothing polls the deploy or verifies production
health afterwards — do both by hand and report the result: watch the deploy through to
completion, then hit the production health check from the `## Deploy Configuration` section in
CLAUDE.md. If production comes back unhealthy, revert the merge commit rather than fixing
forward, and tell me before you do anything else.
blocks.surrounding_prose: Gated by: '(only if you took the manual path at step 13)'. This block invokes no skill/agent — it is manual merge instructions using `gh pr checks` / `gh pr merge` directly, contrasted against land-and-deploy which is named descriptively (as not running on this path), not invoked here. References content-qa and doc-verifier (already run earlier) and CLAUDE.md's Deploy Configuration section. Followed by a horizontal rule '---' ending the step.
